fixes.explanation: Armies it is, friend. Jabin, king of Hazor, sent word to the other kings, and they "…came out with all their armies, a multitude as numerous as the sand on the seashore…" (Joshua 11:1, 4). Kings from the mountains, the foothills, the Arabah and beyond all showed up. You know how hard it is to get a whole family to agree on one dinner time? These kings got ALL those armies to one place!

Close, friend, but those names come from the verse right before. Verse 21 says Joshua eliminated the Anakim from the hill country of Hebron, Debir and Anab. The survivors come in verse 22: Gaza, Gath and Ashdod. Two verses back to back, like two cookie tins that look the same. Easy to reach for the first tin on the shelf.

Jericho, Ai and Bethel are names you might know from other parts of Joshua, but they aren't in this list. Joshua 11:22 says the Anakim who survived were in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod. Those three are the only ones named here. When a verse hands you a short list, stick to the list, friend.

problems.problem: The passage says Jabin sent word to the kings, but it does not say that one message went out.
Papa describes himself sending a group text. Phones should come up as things other people use, not as part of his own world.
“You just grabbed the wrong tin” calls the baker’s answer wrong.
The drawer joke does not make a clear connection between being famous and being listed, so it fails the joke logic test.
